title: RMST Inference from Current-Status Data When Inspection Density Vanishes at the Horizon
banked_reason: D0.5.G delivered tier=subfield below the field floor: paper_score_ceiling 6.8 < 7.4; typed math review passed, and the only unrepaired item is closest-prior-art positioning that cannot lift the tier.
gap_reasons: Delivered tier subfield < floor field; not salvageable within scope.
The contribution is the explicit Bernoulli interval and its fixed-class guarantees, not a new phase transition or finite-sample optimal interval.
The paper proves worst-case expected-length orders but gives no realized-design length optimality or practical length comparison with likelihood-based and optimized conditional intervals.
positioning_omits_closest_prior_art@thm:cell-coverage remained unrepaired: Kim, Fay & Proschan (2021) must be acknowledged as the closest pointwise current-status confidence-interval comparison.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved the explicit spacing-plus-endpoint-polynomial interval, finite-sample design-conditional coverage, and matching fixed-class minimax MSE and expected-length rates, then strengthened the result to show that unknown population weights cost no rate under independent-fold conditioning. The typed math review passed, but the cold referee capped the contribution at subfield because the phase transition has adjacent prior art and the run supplied neither realized-design length optimality nor practical comparator evidence. A future re-raise must add a materially new result or empirical program and must distinguish Kim, Fay & Proschan (2021), rather than merely retrying the same scope.
tldr: The spacing and endpoint-polynomial interval gives finite-sample design-conditional RMST coverage under measurable polynomial endpoint thinning. On the fixed nonempty monotone Hölder class, known and unknown population-weight procedures attain matching minimax MSE and honest expected-length orders in all three regimes. The unknown-weight interval conditions on the independent second-fold design and estimates stratum weights on the first fold.
gap: Established RMST and current-status asymptotics do not settle exact design-conditional coverage under a merely measurable density that vanishes at the horizon. General weak-overlap theory gives the rate mechanism in a different function class, and conditional Gaussian modulus theory does not evaluate this Bernoulli diffuse-integral problem.
fill: Establish the explicit spacing and endpoint-polynomial interval, prove its conditional coverage and matching fixed-class minimax risk and expected-length orders, and test practical constants against optimized conditional and likelihood-based baselines.
